design_rationale: The study explicitly states that pregnant women were included in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial and were allocated to one of three intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment is stated and measured background characteristics were broadly comparable, the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and baseline serum ferritin differed significantly between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pregnant women were included in a randomized, double-blind trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: A double-dummy design successfully masked treatment, compliance was similar across groups, and treatment failures and additional iron use were retained in intention-to-treat analyses with a sensitivity analysis showing unchanged findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment failures were included in the main analyses according to the ‘intention to treat’ principle; dropouts were included until the time of dropout.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only about 77%–82% of participants had complete end-of-study data, and although missingness was reportedly balanced across groups, no analysis established that outcomes were unbiased by missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Missing data mainly due to non attendance were evenly distributed between groups throughout the study and at the end of the study there were complete data from 24 (77%), 24 (82%) and 23 (79%) women in the HI, Non-HI and the placebo group respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The principal hematologic and iron-status outcomes were objective laboratory measures obtained identically across groups in a quality-controlled laboratory, making differential assessment unlikely despite caretakers having access to Hb values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were performed in the Laboratory of Clinical Biochemistry in Haukeland University Hospital, regularly undergoing quality controls within international programs.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while numerous laboratory outcomes, time points, pairwise comparisons, and subgroup analyses created scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood samples from all participants were analyzed at entry (before the 13th week), in weeks 19–21, 27–29, 37–39, 6–10 weeks postpartum (pp) and half a year pp for the following parameters: Red cell indices (Hb, erythrocytes, hematocrit, MCV, MCH, MCHC), reticulocytes, s-iron, Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC), s-ferritin and erythrocyte protoporphyrin (E-PP).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by absent reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment, approximately 18%–23% incomplete outcome data without a robust missing-data analysis, and lack of a reported protocol or prespecified analysis plan. Blinding, objective laboratory outcome measurement, balanced compliance, and intention-to-treat-oriented analyses reduce concern in the other domains.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that eligible pregnant women were randomly allocated to receive daily ferrous sulfate or placebo, so it is classified as a randomized trial despite the absence of details on sequence generation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation was stated, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and age differed significantly between groups at baseline.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The groups did not differ significantly in weight, height, BMI, or gestational age, but the difference in age was significant.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and relevant personnel were blinded with indistinguishable placebo tablets, but adherence, protocol deviations, and use of an intention-to-treat analysis were not reported; the unequal analyzed group sizes and reported abortions further obscure the analysis population.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The physician, laboratory analysts, and subjects were not aware of the type of tablet.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome tables use the randomized group denominators, but participant flow and outcome-specific completeness are not explicitly documented, while four abortions imply that at least some delivery outcomes could not have been observed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We found one case of pregnancy-induced hypertension and three cases of abortion in the iron group and one case of abortion in the placebo group (data not shown).

domain_judgments.rationale: Maternal biomarkers and birth outcomes were measured identically across groups using objective methods, and laboratory analysts and participants were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemoglobin concentration was measured with a Coulter electronic counter, model K-800. Serum ferritin was measured by a radioimmunoassay with a Gamacounter, model 1001.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a trial registration identifier is provided, the text does not establish prospective registration or a prespecified analysis plan, and multiple outcomes, time points, and statistical methods created opportunities for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Independent t-tests were used to compare the baseline quantitative characteristics. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare the main quantitative outcomes with adjustment for the confounder baseline variables. Repeated measures were used to compare the main quantitative outcomes several times throughout the study.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The trial was blinded and used objective outcome measurements, but sequence generation and allocation concealment, adherence and analysis-set handling, completeness of delivery outcomes, and prospective outcome/analysis specification were insufficiently reported.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated using a computer-generated randomization schedule prepared by an independent consultant, so the study is a randomized controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated by an independent consultant, implemented through sequentially coded opaque bottles prepared by the pharmacy, and measured baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-generated randomization schedule, with balanced blocks and stratified for parity ... was generated by an independent consultant. Opaque bottles with childproof lids were marked with a sequential, numerical code and were filled according to the randomization schedule by the Pharmacy Department.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were blinded with indistinguishable placebo tablets, adherence was similar between groups, protocol-directed concomitant high-dose iron was documented, and all available data were analyzed according to randomized assignment using intention-to-treat analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial participants and the research team were unaware of the group assignment... Placebo tablets, which were identical in color, size, and shape, contained only excipients... All available data were used for intention-to-treat analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome availability was reasonably high but incomplete and somewhat lower in the placebo group, particularly for ferritin at delivery and six-month outcomes; observed characteristics did not differ by missingness, but no sensitivity analysis established that results were robust to potentially informative missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the time of delivery... 186/216 (86%) and 176/214 (82%) ferritin samples were available... At the 6-mo postpartum follow-up... 190/216 (88%) maternal ferritin samples were available... and 177/214 (83%) maternal hemoglobin and ferritin samples were analyzed from the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The principal iron-status outcomes were objective laboratory measures obtained with validated, quality-controlled methods and prespecified diagnostic thresholds, while blinding minimized differential measurement of both laboratory and self-reported outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemoglobin concentrations were measured spectrophotometrically by using a Cell Dyn 4000 analyzer... and serum ferritin was determined by a microparticle enzyme immunoassay... Quality controls were used to check the accuracy of the analytic methods.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes and statistical methods were described, but no prospective registration or publicly available analysis plan was reported, and numerous outcome measures and time points leave some scope for selective reporting or analysis choice.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes were the incidence of maternal IDA at delivery, maternal iron status at 6 mo postpartum, and gastrointestinal side effects at 24 and 36 wk of gestation.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Randomization, blinding, adherence, and objective outcome measurement were strong, but incomplete outcome data without sensitivity analyses and the absence of a reported prospective protocol or analysis plan create some concern about missingness and selective reporting.

design_rationale: The 275 eligible iron-replete, nonanemic women were explicitly allocated to iron or placebo using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used and allocation was concealed by a non-patient-facing data manager; although prepregnancy weight and ferritin differed at baseline, the few imbalances among many measured characteristics are compatible with chance and adjusted analyses did not materially alter results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women were randomly allocated to treatment groups on the basis of random numbers generated by the study data manager using a computerized algorithm (STATVIEW II; Abacus Concepts, Inc, Berkeley, California).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were blinded with indistinguishable capsules, adherence before 28 weeks was similar between groups, and outcomes were analyzed according to randomized assignment; protocol-driven treatment changes after 28 weeks applied to both groups and were part of the intended strategy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The data manager (who did not have contact with patients) assigned participants to their groups and held the link. WIC personnel, laboratory analysts, and patients were not aware of the type of capsules.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial outcome data were missing (28.7% for third-trimester iron status and 22.5% for birth weight), and missingness was associated with gestational age at entry and race, although rates and reasons were similar by group and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses supported the low-birth-weight finding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seventy-nine women (28.7%) were missing data on third-trimester iron status, 62 (22.5%) were missing data on infant birth weight, and 43 (15.6%) were missing data on both.

domain_judgments.rationale: Birth weight and hematologic outcomes were objective and measured consistently using program records and standardized laboratory methods, with laboratory analysts blinded to assignment; gestational age based on reported last menstrual period is less accurate but unlikely to be differentially mismeasured by group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: WIC personnel, laboratory analysts, and patients were not aware of the type of capsules.

domain_judgments.rationale: Birth weight and gestational-age outcomes were added during the study, and numerous related birth outcomes and analytical definitions were examined without a reported preregistered analysis plan, creating substantial scope for selective outcome and analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the study, we added birth weight and gestational age as outcomes because of a need for more information on the functional consequences of iron supplementation during pregnancy.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the prominent birth outcomes were introduced during the trial and evaluated through multiple related outcomes and definitions without a reported prespecified analysis plan. Substantial missing outcome data add some concerns despite balanced attrition and supportive multiple-imputation analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned 1:1 using package numbers linked to a statistician-prepared random-number chart, with allocation masked until primary analyses were completed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated from a random-number chart by an independent statistician, implemented through consecutively issued numbered packages, and concealed by masking until study completion; reported baseline characteristics were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Taiyuan Satellite Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. prepared equal quantities of iron or placebo capsules and folate capsules and assigned 4-digit package numbers beginning with 0001 according to a random-number chart prepared by a statistician who was not part of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, personnel, and investigators were masked and primary analyses used intention-to-treat, but physicians could prescribe medicinal iron and participants could independently obtain iron-containing supplements, with incomplete information about these potential deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Physicians were free to use clinical judgment in treating anemic women... Women were free to obtain over-the-counter iron-containing supplements on their own, regardless of group assignment or whether or not they were anemic.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 31% of randomized participants lacked outcome data, and although attrition rates and stated reasons were similar by group, the amount of missingness was substantial and participants lost because they delivered elsewhere could not be shown to have outcomes unrelated to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Attrition affected the groups similarly both in proportion [31.8% (377 of 1186) in the placebo/folate group and 30.5% (362 of 1185) in the iron/folate group] and reason.

domain_judgments.rationale: Maternal and neonatal iron outcomes were objective laboratory measurements collected and analyzed with the same standardized procedures across masked groups, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study participants, personnel, and investigators were unaware of supplement group. The code was not broken until the study and primary analyses were completed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered only under a listed identifier with no prospectively dated protocol or prespecified analysis plan presented, while multiple definitions, time points, outcomes, and adjusted analyses offered scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We defined maternal anemia per WHO guidelines as hemoglobin <110 g/L (1, 2) and ID in the following 2 ways: SF <15 mg/L (14) and body iron (BI) <0 mg/kg (15).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because roughly 31% of randomized participants lacked outcome data, without sufficient evidence that the reported treatment effects were robust to potentially outcome-dependent missingness. Additional concerns arise from permitted nonstudy iron use and limited evidence of prospective outcome/analysis specification.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly describe the study as randomized and report allocation to iron or placebo, so RoB 2 applies.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial is described as randomized and the groups were comparable on reported baseline characteristics, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The design of the study was randomised, double-blind, placebo controlled.

domain_judgments.rationale: Despite nominal double blinding, tablet consumption differed markedly between groups, potentially revealing assignment and indicating substantial differential adherence, while no intention-to-treat analysis or strategy addressing deviations is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The number of tablets consumed per person was mean 159 ± 38 (SD) in the iron treated group and 93 ± 43 in the placebo treated group (p < 0.001).

domain_judgments.rationale: Forty-one of 248 enrolled women were excluded after allocation based partly on post-randomization pregnancy complications and uncomplicated delivery was required for final inclusion, creating substantial potential for attrition bias even though exclusion frequencies were said not to differ significantly.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 248 females, 20 placebo and 21 iron treated were excluded for the following causes: withdrawn consent, 10; uterine bleeding episodes, 5; placental insufficiency, placenta praevia and abruptio placentae, 7; praeoclampsia, 3; partus praematurus, 5; excessive smoking (≥10 cigarettes/day), 3.

domain_judgments.rationale: The principal iron-status outcomes were objective laboratory measurements obtained repeatedly and assessed using the same stated methods in both randomized groups, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In all 207 females, Hb and red cell volume (MCV) were determined on Coulter-S ... and S-HPL by radioimmunoassay.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes, time points, thresholds, and alternative definitions were analyzed, leaving scope for selective reporting despite extensive tabulation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: If iron deficiency anaemia was defined as S-ferritin ≤15 μg/l and Hb <110 g/l, 3% of the females were anaemic. If S-ferritin <12 μg/l and Hb <110 g/l were chosen as limits, none of the females in the iron treated group displayed anaemia.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial differential adherence without a reported intention-to-treat approach and by post-randomization exclusion of 41 participants based partly on pregnancy complications and delivery status. Randomization methods and outcome-selection safeguards were also incompletely reported.
